## ***Registered learners are up 23% year over year, and Professional Certificate enrollments have doubled, as universities bring global courses into their degree programs.***


This week, at the Third International Forum of Strategic Partners in Astana, we announced an exciting milestone: Kazakhstan has surpassed one million registered learners on Coursera. Our Q3 2026 data shows registered learners up 23% year over year, alongside growing enrollments in Specializations and Professional Certificates.


The news comes as Kazakhstan expands its international education partnerships and works toward its ambition of becoming the academic hub of Eurasia. Over the past four years, Coursera has partnered with more than 100 universities across the country. With the help of our local partner, Bilim Upskill, participating institutions are integrating courses into their degree programs, so students can earn academic credit while building job-ready skills in artificial intelligence, data science, business, and more.


To me, reaching one million learners reflects Kazakhstan’s deep commitment to expanding access to world-class education. Universities are giving students more opportunities to build industry-relevant skills alongside their degrees, and we’re proud to support Kazakhstan’s students and universities as they build skills for the jobs of tomorrow.


That commitment starts at the top. Under the leadership of Sayasat Nurbek, Minister of Science and Higher Education, Kazakhstan is modernizing higher education, growing international partnerships, and bringing global learning resources into university curricula. This work supports the country’s Higher Education Development Concept for 2023–2029, which prioritizes internationalization, lifelong learning, workforce readiness, digital skills, and educational infrastructure.


Speaking at the Forum, Minister Nurbek put it this way: “We are ready to experiment. The biggest risk is not taking any risks at all. We must be willing to try new things, including innovative partnerships such as our collaboration with Coursera. And the growing number of partners at this Third International Forum of Strategic Partners demonstrates our ambition to position Kazakhstan as the academic hub of Eurasia.”


**Sayasat Nurbek, Kazakhstan’s Minister of Science and Higher Education** , *addressing attendees at the Third International Forum of Strategic Partners in Astana*


## **Kazakhstan’s learning trends on Coursera**


Beyond the headline number, a few trends in the data stand out:


- **More learners are pursuing structured, career-focused learning.** Specialization enrollments grew 89% year over year, while Professional Certificate enrollments doubled. (Q3 2026 vs. Q3 2025)
- **Demand spans technical and non-technical fields.** STEM Specialization enrollments rose 87%, and non-STEM Specialization enrollments grew 91%. (Q3 2026 vs. Q3 2025)
- **AI and human skills development gives the country a benchmark for progress.** Kazakhstan ranks 55th among 98 countries in our[AI-Human Skills Synergy Index](https://www.coursera.org/skills-reports/global) , which looks at how populations are building AI and human skills alongside broader national AI readiness.


## **How universities in Kazakhstan are putting Coursera to work**


Universities at the Forum shared how they’re using Coursera to open up new learning opportunities:


- **Al-Farabi Kazakh National University** is upskilling teachers and creating courses for its students. It’s now developing courses for a global audience as Coursera’s first content partner in Kazakhstan.
- **Khoja Akhmet Yassawi International Kazakh-Turkish University** is using Coursera’s exam proctoring capabilities for more than 2,000 students to support academic integrity in online education.
- **Kh. Dosmukhamedov Atyrau University** is integrating Professional Certificates into university programs in areas like sports performance and nutrition, UI/UX design, data analytics, and talent development for HR professionals, aligning learning with industry needs.


*Coursera and Bilim Upskill teams at the Third International Forum of Strategic Partners in Astana*


The momentum isn’t limited to higher education. Businesses and financial institutions across Kazakhstan are also partnering with Coursera to support employee training and workforce development.


I’m grateful to every university, partner, and learner who helped Kazakhstan reach this milestone, and I look forward to what comes next.


To learn more about Coursera’s learning programs, visit[coursera.org](https://www.coursera.org/) .
